public_rationale: The evidence supports uncertainty about productivity estimates and reports operational strain associated with AI adoption. It also records likely productivity gains and faster deployments. Those benefits do not resolve general net effects, while the reported burdens do not establish that excess generated code caused companies' difficulties. The full causal claim remains unsettled.
limitations: METR's study population does not represent all companies.
Harness commissioned the survey and sells tools addressing the reported problems.
Self-reported associations cannot establish the causal mechanism or net effect.
The outcome would differ if the claim meant only that some companies experienced added review work.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The actual economic or productivity effects of coding LLMs are unclear, other than an abundance of new code that is making running companies harder.

our_interpretation: Use 2026 Q1, the latest completed quarter before publication, to assess the contemporaneous evidence and company conditions.
Read the first component as uncertainty about general net economic and productivity effects, rather than a claim that no individual task benefit has been measured.
Read the second component as a broader causal assertion that increased generated-code volume imposes operational burdens on companies.
One company's experience can establish an example, but cannot alone establish the broader characterization.
Faster deployment, added review work, and net company productivity are distinct outcomes.
criteria.support_condition: Credible evidence shows that general net effects remained unsettled and that increased generated-code volume caused material review, maintenance, security, or coordination burdens across relevant companies.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Robust, broadly applicable evidence settles the general net effects, or representative causal evidence refutes the claimed operational burden from increased code volume.

evidence.explanation: A February survey of 700 enterprise engineering practitioners and managers reports greater downstream burdens among frequent AI users, alongside faster deployments. It supports reported operational strain but does not isolate increased code volume as its cause.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Representative company evidence linking measured generated-code growth to downstream burdens, with credible controls and measurement of offsetting productivity gains, plus a synthesis of net effects known in the target period.
